exposure: practice of waiting for a minimum number of children to open an MCV vial
requesting payment for a home-based record (HBR)
caregiver knowledge about needing two doses
outcome: MCV2 doses administered (according to different sources)
agreement between register and home-based record for MCV2 status
drop-out differences between first and second doses of MCV
cohort: The study included health facilities and households with children who had received more than one vaccination in 6 low-performing districts in Malawi.
finding: The study found high and inconsistent drop-out rates between the first and second doses of MCV, poor quality of administrative data, and that session cancellation, charging for home-based records, and lack of caregiver knowledge negatively impacted the completion of the vaccination series.
cross-section timing: The study was performed after the introduction of a second routine dose of measles containing vaccine (MCV2) in 2015, likely around 2020 as indicated by the abstract ID.
